title: sega.com, from “It’s Thinking” to “In memory”
lede: Screenshots of pages saved by the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, stored as images. Click one to open the original capture. dreamcast.com itself was archived in this period, but its images were not saved, so these are from sega.com and sega.net.[^27]

snips.text: A “View A Game” menu listing the launch-window catalogue: **NFL 2K**, **Sonic Adventure**, **Soul Calibur**, **Power Stone**, **Hydro Thunder**, **Ready 2 Rumble** and more.
“Get updated on SegaNet before the launch on 9.7.00.”
“**In memory Isao Okawa 1926–2001**” above “Tired of waiting? Play online now!”

note: Flash elements in these pages no longer run and were removed before the screenshots were taken; some banner images were never archived and show as empty boxes.

captures.label: It’s Thinking
captures.title: A month after launch
captures.text: The U.S. home page five weeks after 9/9/99, with the “It’s Thinking” tagline, a game picker and links to the console and the store. The Flash banner at the left is missing.

captures.label: Get connected
captures.title: Selling the modem
captures.text: Virtua Tennis on one side, SegaNet on the other, and a $50 online bonus badge. The price cut to $149 came two weeks later.[^15]

captures.label: SegaNet
captures.title: The countdown to 9.7.00
captures.text: The teaser page for Sega’s internet service, three weeks before it opened.

captures.label: Jet Grind Radio
captures.title: One week before the PlayStation 2
captures.text: The home page leads with Jet Grind Radio. Sony’s console reached U.S. stores on October 26.[^7]

captures.label: In memory
captures.title: After the exit
captures.text: Ten weeks after the announcement, the page carries a memorial line for Isao Okawa and a new link, “What’s up at Sega?”
